summary: Reserves an additional, larger IPv6 prefix, a /20, for use in documentation, expanding on 2001:db8::/32 from RFC 3849. This lets examples reflect realistic deployments for large networks. It updates RFC 3849.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9637 reserves a larger IPv6 prefix for documentation. It lets examples describe larger networks while directing that the prefix not be used for real traffic.

questions: what ipv6 prefix is for documentation
what does rfc 9637 change in rfc 3849
subtitle: Reserves 3fff::/20 as a larger IPv6 prefix for documentation examples.

tldr.problem: The existing 2001:db8::/32 documentation prefix was inadequate for many realistic IPv6 deployment examples.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC reserves the 3fff::/20 prefix from the Global Unicast Address pool for documentation and registers it with IANA.
tldr.outcome: The prefix is for examples only; it must not be used for actual traffic or globally advertised.

today: RFC 9637 is an Informational document that updates RFC 3849. The unit metadata does not list it as obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why More Documentation Space Was Needed
sections.content:
RFC 3849 reserved 2001:db8::/32 for IPv6 documentation. The original block was intended to reduce conflicts between examples and deployed systems.

The RFC says growing IPv6 network size and diversity made the original prefix inadequate for many realistic scenarios. Without another block, documentation might use space already allocated to organizations or drawn from the unallocated pool.
sections.plainLanguage: The existing documentation prefix was too small for some examples. Using real or unallocated address space could cause conflicts.

sections.title: Why the Prefix Is a /20
sections.content:
The RFC cites Regional Internet Registry data from August 2023. Of 62,770 recorded IPv6 unicast allocations and assignments, 25.9% were larger than a /32, and a /29 was the most common size at 24.8%.

The four largest assignments to end users were /19s, made before the RIRs moved away from a fixed /48 site prefix. The RFC says it is unlikely that individual networks will need more than a /20 in the foreseeable future and believes this size covers documentation needs.
sections.plainLanguage: The authors used reported allocation sizes to choose a prefix large enough for documentation of realistic network deployments.

sections.title: Appropriate Use and IANA Registration
sections.content:
Documentation prefixes are for configuration and documentation examples. They must not be used for actual traffic or globally advertised, and should not be used for routed production traffic or other connectivity. The RFC says they should be treated as bogons and filtered in routing advertisements as appropriate.

IANA registered 3fff::/20 as Documentation in the IPv6 Special-Purpose Address Registry. The entry marks it as not a source, destination, forwardable or globally reachable address.
sections.plainLanguage: Use this prefix in examples, not on production networks. The registry records that it is not globally reachable or forwardable.

references.text: Huston, G., Lord, A., and P. Smith, "IPv6 Address Prefix Reserved for Documentation", RFC 3849, July 2004.
